subject: Aurora: incident closure, exec assurance & follow-through
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Samir.Patel <samir.patel@aurora.com>, Tina.Cho <tina.cho@aurora.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-04T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Aurora service incident — RCA deliverable + proposed corrective actions

Hi Samir / Tina,

Attached is our formal RCA and the commitments register for the May 2nd service disruption you experienced. High-level summary below for your exec team:

Summary (tl;dr)
- Impact: elevated 95th pct latency (250–900ms) and increased 5xx error rate for text-generation endpoints during the 09:40–10:55 UTC window on May 2; throughput dropped intermittently due to backpressure.
- Root causes (multi-factor):
  1) Model kernel fallback: a sudden model shard scheduling decision led to a slower execution kernel for several hosts when sequence length exceeded 1k tokens.
  2) KV cache eviction storm: unexpected input patterns triggered aggressive KV eviction causing cache thrash and higher token-recompute rates.
  3) Autoscaler policy gap: burst autoscaler thresholds were conservative for your traffic profile and did not trigger additional reserved capacity early enough.

Action summary (attached commitments spreadsheet has owners & JIRA links):
- Short-term (72 hours): pin tolerant kernel variant for critical routes, enable soft-KV-preserve to reduce eviction, temporarily increase burst headroom for your dedicated pool. Owner: Kimberly Park (engineering).
- Mid-term (2 weeks): rollout optimized kernel selection logic that considers observed seq-length distribution; improve telemetry to expose per-route KV eviction metrics. Owner: Karthik Iyer (runtime).
- Long-term (quarter): update autoscaler policy templates for priority accounts and add an automated pre-warm for predicted traffic spikes. Owner: Jonas Weber (platform).

Attachments: aurora_rca_050428.pdf (full RCA), aurora_commitments_050428.xlsx (owner matrix).

Request: please confirm an exec readout time for this week — we propose Tuesday 17:00 ET for a 30-minute alignment and sign-off on the commitments register. We will also share a single-pane status board and weekly cadence.

Thanks — apologies again for the customer impact. We want to ensure full transparency and concrete timelines.

— Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: aurora_rca_050428.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)]
[Attachment: aurora_commitments_050428.xlsx (XLSX, 52KB)]

We can do Tuesday 17:00 ET — prefer a short readout (30 minutes).

Samir / Laura / team,

Thanks — adding a concise assurance note and an explicit fallback plan below. I've attached the commitments spreadsheet (sheet: owner-tasks) which calls out JIRA tasks.

One-page exec assurance (for your CTO):
- What happened: kernel selection + KV eviction + autoscaler gap produced transient latency and elevated 5xx.
- Immediate containment: pinned tolerant kernel for affected routes; enabled soft-KV-preserve; increased burst headroom by +25% on your pool. (Completed 05/04 11:00 PT)
- Canary plan: 10% traffic canary for kernel variant for 48 hours with 1-minute SLO guard rails — automatic rollback on breach of error/latency thresholds.
- Fallback commitment: automatic rollback to prior kernel and burst headroom restore within 90s of SLO breach; we will also cut traffic to a lower-cost path if required.
- Timeline: short-term mitigations live; mid-term code delivery targeted 2028-05-16; autoscaler policy template rollout targeted 2028-05-30.

Owners and JIRA links (top items):
- OPS-782: implement canary + auto-rollback (Owner: Jonas Weber)
- RUNTIME-1293: KV-preserve tuning + telemetry (Owner: Karthik Iyer)
- KERNEL-447: kernel selection heuristics (Owner: Kimberly Park)

Attachments: aurora_commitments_050428.xlsx (owner matrix, canary schedule).

Laura — I will be at the Tuesday 17:00 ET readout to run the technical portion and own the rollback mechanics.

— Kimberly Park
Sr. Prod Eng Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Laura / Kimberly —

Quick update from Aurora execs: CTO reviewed the one-page assurance and the commitments register. We appreciate the clear rollback language and the canary configuration — that addressed our immediate governance concerns.

Status:
- Canary completed (48 hours) with no sustained SLO breaches; minor spikes during the first 2 hours were automatically rolled back and re-applied after a config tweak.
- Aurora is satisfied with the short-term remediation and asks that the mid-term kernel selection change and autoscaler policy be prioritized.
- Procurement has requested a short amendment to our SLA to include a temporary elevated burst headroom clause for priority accounts until the autoscaler policy change is complete — procurement@aurora.com will follow up with a DocuSign link.

Request: please continue weekly status notes for two additional weeks (next update requested 2028-05-18). After that, we will evaluate for formal closure.

Thanks for the responsiveness — this helped restore confidence quickly.

— Tina Cho
Head of IT Operations
Aurora Commerce
